<target>## **2.7. Explicit Accesses to CSRs Wider than XLEN**

If a standard CSR is wider than XLEN bits, then an explicit read of the CSR returns the register’s leastsignificant XLEN bits, and an explicit write to the CSR modifies only the register’s least-significant XLEN bits, leaving the upper bits unchanged.

Some standard CSRs, such as the counter CSRs of extension Zicntr, are always 64 bits, even when XLEN=32 (RV32). For each such 64-bit CSR (for example, counter `time` ), a corresponding 32-bit _high-_

_half CSR_ is usually defined with the same name but with the letter ‘h’ appended at the end ( `timeh` ). The high-half CSR aliases bits 63:32 of its namesake 64-bit CSR, thus providing a way for RV32 software to read and modify the otherwise-unreachable 32 bits.

Standard high-half CSRs are accessible only when the base RISC-V instruction set is RV32 (XLEN=32). For RV64 (when XLEN=64), the addresses of all standard high-half CSRs are reserved, so an attempt to access a high-half CSR typically raises an illegal-instruction exception.</target>
